title: Cloud platform / infrastructure
transcript:
Platform Engineering Lead: Alright, let's dive into the cloud strategy options. First, I've got a proposal for a hybrid approach, combining AWS and Google Cloud.

SRE: Hold on a sec, haven't we considered the complexities of managing multiple cloud providers before?

Platform Engineering Lead: Yes, I understand your concern, but hear me out. The hybrid approach would significantly reduce our overall maintenance load.

Finance Partner: And what about the long-term costs? We're trying to minimize expenses here.

Platform Engineering Lead: That's a valid concern, but the hybrid approach allows us to leverage Google Cloud's Machine Learning APIs, accelerating time-to-value and offering advanced AI capabilities.

CTO: I see the benefits, but we should also consider the potential increased costs associated with this hybrid approach.

SRE: Plus, managing multiple clouds might lead to operational nightmares down the line.

Platform Engineering Lead: I agree that it's not without its challenges, but I believe the benefits outweigh the drawbacks. With this approach, we can build a custom analytics platform on AWS, which fits better with our existing infrastructure.

CTO: Alright, let's table this for a moment. I'd like to revisit the other options before we make a decision.

Finance Partner: Building an entirely custom cloud platform seems like a high-maintenance load and has a prohibitive time-to-value.

SRE: And purchasing a commercial cloud platform would lack the required custom analytics features and wouldn't meet regulatory compliance.

CTO: Building a custom analytics platform on Google Cloud would result in higher long-run maintenance costs and limited integration with our existing AWS services.

Platform Engineering Lead: Given these considerations, it seems the hybrid approach offers the best balance.

CTO: Agreed, but we must ensure compliance with all AWS and Google Cloud security and regulatory standards.

Finance Partner: And additional costs for integrating and managing the hybrid system may arise.

Platform Engineering Lead: I'll take ownership of the platform. If we move forward, I'll work closely with the SRE team to mitigate the complexities.

CTO: I see no other objections. I'm signing off on the decision. Hybrid approach it is.

SRE: Just remember, the complexity is still a concern, but I'll do my best to work around it.

CTO: Understood. Let's move on to the next agenda item. (off-topic exchange, 2 turns)

SRE: By the way, have you heard about the new gaming console that just launched?

Finance Partner: Oh, yes! I pre-ordered one. Can't wait to try it out.

(Return to the topic)

CTO: Alright, back to business. Let's outline the plan for implementing this hybrid approach. Platform Engineering Lead, can you start us off?

Platform Engineering Lead: Absolutely. I'll work on a detailed plan and present it at our next meeting.

Title: Platform Engineering Decision - Custom Analytics Platform

The team has decided to adopt a hybrid approach for the development of the custom analytics platform. This will involve building the core platform on AWS, while leveraging Google Cloud's machine learning services for advanced AI capabilities. This strategy offers a better fit with our existing infrastructure, reduces overall maintenance load, and provides a smoother transition.

To ensure compliance with both AWS and Google Cloud security and regulatory standards, the charity will implement necessary measures. While there may be additional costs associated with integrating and managing the hybrid system, these are outweighed by the benefits.

The decision was reached after considering various options, including building an entirely custom cloud platform, purchasing a commercial cloud platform, and building a custom analytics platform on Google Cloud alone. The hybrid approach offers the optimal balance between time-to-value, maintenance load, and advanced AI capabilities.
